claims.text: The identity of X governs whether CrFeCoNiX forms a stable, coherent protective oxide during high-temperature exposure.
Al promotes formation of a continuous, dense, slow-growing, adherent Al2O3-containing scale on CrFeCoNiAl.
Si promotes formation of a continuous, dense, slow-growing, adherent silica-rich scale on CrFeCoNiSi.
Mn forms comparatively volatile and less stable oxides on CrFeCoNiMn.
Mn-containing scales are mixed or porous and therefore prone to cracking or spallation under thermal stress.
Oxide-scale microstructure and alloy phase composition mediate protective behavior.
Al has high oxygen affinity and sufficiently low high-temperature diffusivity to produce a slow-growing diffusion-barrier scale.
Si has high oxygen affinity and sufficiently low high-temperature diffusivity to produce a slow-growing diffusion-barrier scale.
Mn forms mixed-valence, porous oxides that fail to hinder continued oxidation.
Failure to hinder oxidation produces thermal-mismatch stresses and scale spallation in the Mn-containing alloy.
Under identical exposure, CrFeCoNiAl and CrFeCoNiSi will form thinner, more coherent and adherent scales than CrFeCoNiMn.
CrFeCoNiMn will exhibit thicker, cracked or spalled scales under the specified exposure.
CrFeCoNi without an added X element will form a mixed, less protective oxide than the Al- or Si-containing alloys.
The proposed behavior applies above 900 °C in oxidative or moderately corrosive atmospheres.
Secondary phases and processing-induced microstructural changes can alter oxide-scale characteristics.
Multiphase alloy microstructures may alter local oxidation behavior.
